unit.title: Helpers that act: steps, tools and asking first

lesson.title: Ask first!
lesson.subtitle: Why a helper asks before it acts, and you decide

video.title: Ask first!
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Amina Bello — primary teacher, Nigeria (main character)
Ms Salma Haddad — secondary maths teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice, talking to the student (warm, peer to peer)

chapters.label: The app checks too, and secrets

scenes.visual: A list: Sent too soon; A mistake!; Today’s rule.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Imagine a helper that sends a message to your whole class group before anyone says yes. What if it has a mistake in it? You can’t take it back! That’s why today’s rule matters.

scenes.animation: The Darsi mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: the most important rule for helpers: ask first!

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Looking is fine; doing needs a yes
scenes.narration: Some jobs only look things up, like the weather. That’s fine without asking. But some jobs do things: send a message, buy something, or delete a photo. Those need your yes first.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Watch Darsi Tiny. I asked it to send a message to Mrs Mensah: the trip to the farm is cancelled. It didn’t send it. It asked: shall I send this message? Please reply yes or no.

scenes.visual: A list: Read the message; The right person?; The right words?; Then say yes or no.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Before you say yes, read the message. Is it for the right person? Are the words right? Only then say yes, or no.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Quick check! The helper asks: shall I send “Football is cancelled” to the whole school? But it’s only your class’s match. What do you say?

scenes.visual: A list: Wrong group: say no; No is always allowed; Fix it, then it asks again.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: No: it would go to the wrong group. Saying no is always allowed. You can fix the message, and let it ask again.

scenes.visual: A list: Only “Yes, send it”; A made-up message!; The app blocks it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Helpers can get this wrong. Someone typed only “Yes, send it”, and Darsi Tiny made up a message to send! So the app checks too, and blocks what nobody said yes to.

scenes.visual: A list: Never your password; No private things; Strange? Tell a grown-up.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Some things are never for helpers: your password, or private things about you or your friends. If a helper does something strange, stop and tell a grown-up.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, ask Darsi Tiny to send the message to Mrs Mensah. Say no first, then try again and say yes. Nothing really leaves the phone: it’s practice.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Your turn. Which job needs your yes first: checking the weather, or buying a game?

scenes.visual: Summary points: Doing things needs a yes; Read first; no is OK; Passwords stay secret.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Doing things needs a yes · Read first; no is OK · Passwords stay secret
scenes.narration: Buying a game: it spends money. Remember: looking things up is fine, but doing things needs a yes. Read before you say yes, and no is always allowed. Passwords stay secret.

scenes.visual: A list: Play “Yes or No”; The helper asks first; You say yes or no, and why.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it yourself: play Yes or No with your family. Someone plays a helper and asks before doing things. You say yes or no, and why!

checkpoints.prompt: The helper asks: shall I send “Football is cancelled” to the whole school? But it’s only your class’s match. What do you say?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — the message would go to the wrong group. Saying no is always allowed, and you can fix it first.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — read who it is for. It’s the wrong group, so say no, and fix it.

checkpoints.prompt: Which job needs your yes first?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — buying a game spends money, so it needs your yes. Checking the weather only looks something up.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — looking things up is fine, but buying something does something: it needs your yes.
